title: E2: E1 retrained on cleaned rows plus joint government advisories and Atomic Red Team tests
question: Do cleaner training rows plus two new labelled sources (author-tagged sentences from joint government advisories, Atomic Red Team test descriptions) raise family recognition, above all on CTI-HAL?
motivation: E1 on CTI-HAL: right family first 0.631, in the top 3 0.816; 178 of 968 statements have the right family outside the top 3, which no answer rule can fix. On dev (not CTI-HAL) only 19 of 118 such misses are rare families; many are noisy or context-dependent labels; real-report sentences gave the largest gains so far (AnnoCTR).

advisories.source: the FBI IC3 copies of joint cybersecurity advisories, https://www.ic3.gov/CSA/2021-2026 (218 listed, 213 downloaded; CISA's own pages refuse automated clients), US government works
advisories.rows: each sentence with a bracketed ATT&CK technique tag, labelled with those ids; tags and tactic/software/footnote brackets removed; leading tactic headings and update markers removed; technique-name list lines, fragments and rows whose family is not listed dropped
advisories.advisories_used: 59 kept; 141 with fewer than 5 tags (guidance notes, FBI-only alerts); 12 excluded because they name a CTI-HAL group (G0008, G0016, G0034, G0037, G0046, G0049, G0102), an ATT&CK alias or software linked to at most two groups including it; 1 (APT40, 2024/240708) excluded for overlapping a held-out text; 5 not downloaded
advisories.count: 765 rows, 155 families (68 repeats and 4 held-out containments dropped)

atomic.rows: '<name>. <description>' without commands, placeholders or technique ids, labelled with the test's technique

cleaning.rules: clean_cases.broken_reason: fragment (< 2 content words), figure caption (caption label and < 10 content words), markdown table row, text naming a technique id, hash table (3+ hashes and < 12 content words); thresholds set by reading dropped training rows only
cleaning.dropped: public train 38 of 6,308 (30 derived procedures naming an id), AnnoCTR train 282 of 1,453 (102 captions, 153 table rows, 18 ids, 9 fragments), ATT&CK procedures 0; dev and test unchanged

data.train: cases_train_clean 6,270 + cases_annoctr_train_clean 1,171 + cases_attack_train_clean 16,273 + cases_advisories_train 765 + cases_atomic_train 1,874 = 26,353 rows (E1: 24,034)
data.checks: 0 CTI-HAL statement texts in either new file; every new row passed the held-out overlap filter of export_attack_procedures

fixed: E1's recipe unchanged: family + technique heads, answer from the 3 most probable families, Cribl adapter + fresh heads, 2 epochs, a checkpoint every quarter epoch, LoRA lr 1e-4, heads 1e-3, 16 per step and per forward pass, seed 7, AnnoCTR rows family loss only (advisory and Atomic rows get both losses); RunPod secure RTX 4090; CTI-HAL scored on the laptop
selection: as E1: the highest mean of public dev exact top-1 and AnnoCTR dev family top-1; ties the earlier

success.headline: CTI-HAL family top-1: E2 minus E1 (same 968 statements), paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
secondary: CTI-HAL exact top-1: E2 minus E1, CI lower bound above 0
AnnoCTR test family top-1: E2 minus E1, CI lower bound above 0
public test family top-1: E2 minus E1, CI lower bound above 0
success.reported: CTI-HAL right family in the top 3 and the count outside it; exact top-3/5; the public test's expert subset separately (advisory-like text); per-source row and drop counts; every checkpoint's dev curve

stop_rules: more than 1% of a split's cases end in error
confirmation_runs: the selected checkpoint once on CTI-HAL, public test and AnnoCTR test; nothing is chosen, refit or rerun because of a confirmation result
adoption: none: an experiment, no product wiring
informed_by: E1's results and dev predictions (docs 21.3.18); the dev analysis of misses outside the top 3; a reading of training rows for the cleaning rules and of 30 advisory rows for label quality; a 10-advisory sample; a laptop pilot (100 rows, 30 dev cases; mechanics only). No E2 model exists.
